headline: SK hynix says its Dalian factory in China is not being expanded and its new equipment has US authorisation, answering a Reuters report of a trade-off for a new US plant.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: the new part is SK hynix's written statement of 16 Oct; the Reuters report and an earlier denial already ran on 15 Oct.
importance_line: It matters to chip buyers, workers and governments in the US, South Korea and China because US limits on tools for Chinese factories are tight, but the original account rests on unnamed sources and SK hynix's statement does not say whether it asked for more tool exports in return for a US factory.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports that SK hynix, the South Korean memory maker, said in a statement on 16 Oct 2026 that no capacity expansion is being sought at the Mod B building of its Dalian factory in China, which was completed in 2023, and that equipment is being installed there in consultation with, and under authorisation from, the US government. This answers the Reuters exclusive we carried in our 15 Oct 2026 edition, which said SK hynix wants Washington to approve more US chipmaking tool exports to the Dalian plant, run by its Solidigm unit, as a condition of building a new US factory; SK hynix had already told Reuters it was not seeking to expand capacity there.
notes: Follow-up of 1015:C08-01 (item 42, 15 Oct 2026 edition). The 15 Oct entry already carried SK hynix's denial to Reuters, so little is new beyond the written statement naming Mod B; the editor may judge it a near-repeat.
